title: Replication with a strong, independently developed public model: CQ500 reference-standard analyses
status: Post hoc relative to the original study. This analysis plan was fixed before model outputs were generated for the evaluation. One scan (CQ500-CT-108) was processed beforehand to measure run time; its output was seen and is reported unchanged.

model.name: CT Head Hemorrhage Detection (MaxViT-Tiny slice encoder + bidirectional GRU)
model.author: Ian Pan
model.training_data: RSNA 2019 Intracranial Hemorrhage Detection data (patient-level split; BHSD subset excluded from classification). CQ500 was not used for training, selection or calibration.
model.inference: HemorrhageSliceModel.predict_hu_volume(volume, batch_size=2, return_segmentation=False, long_series_mode='resample'); fixed class-specific logit blends as released; CPU float32; torch 2.6.0+cpu; timm 1.0.27; no tuning, calibration or threshold selection on CQ500.

input: The 489 CQ500 scans analysed in the locked v2 evaluation; for each, the soft-tissue series chosen by the locked series-selection rule (choose() in research_cq500_extract.py), read with the model's own DICOM loader (rescale slope/intercept applied, slices physically ordered).
reference: CQ500 reader majority (>=2 of 3 readers) for each label; the number of positive reads (0-3) defines agreement strata; batches B1 (consecutive) and B2 (enriched) as released.

scores.subtype: series-level fixed-blend probabilities for epidural, intraparenchymal, intraventricular, subarachnoid and subdural hemorrhage

secondary_descriptive: threshold giving specificity 0.90 among majority-negative scans
threshold giving the specificity of v2 at 1.0 mL (169/284 = 0.595)

endpoints: E1 AUC for any ICH against the reader majority: all 489 scans, B1, B2 (B1-B2 difference by independent bootstrap); AUC restricted to unanimous scans.

E2 Sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV at the primary threshold, overall and by batch; PPV of the B2 operating point at B1 prevalence and the share of the B1-B2 PPV difference attributable to prevalence.

E3 Sensitivity for majority positives decided 2-1 versus 3-0, overall and by number of majority subtype labels (none, one, two or more); Newcombe interval for the difference; two-sided Fisher exact test.
E4 Share at or above the threshold among unanimous negatives versus negatives with one positive read (Newcombe interval).
E5 Cohen's kappa between the model call at the primary threshold and each reader, and between readers on the same scans.

E6 Subtype AUCs against all other scans and within majority ICH-positive scans, using each subtype probability; within ICH-positive scans, compared with the 'any' probability as a type-free baseline (paired DeLong, Holm across five subtypes).
E7 Cross-subtype call matrix at 0.5, off-diagonal cells restricted to scans without the column subtype (as in the original analysis).

E8 BHX and Seg-CQ500 discordances: distribution of the relevant subtype probability (and share >=0.5) in scans with BHX boxes of a subtype but no majority label, versus majority-positive scans and scans with neither; 'any' probability for the two Seg-CQ500 masks on majority-negative scans (CT-108, CT-187). Descriptive; the model is not a reference standard and is not used to adjudicate.
statistics: Wilson intervals for proportions; Newcombe hybrid score intervals for differences; bootstrap percentile intervals (10,000 resamples of scans, seed 20261029) for AUCs and their differences; paired DeLong tests with Holm adjustment for E6; all tests two-sided, alpha 0.05.
interpretation: Findings that replicate with this model are treated as properties of the references that do not depend on probe weakness; differences are reported as model dependence. Agreement of the model with one reference rather than another is reported as uncertainty, not as evidence of which reference is correct.
